old: At its heart sits a verb meaning 'to remember' — but a tiny prefix has quietly taken that away.
In Greek, this word meant simply 'forgetfulness.'
It traveled from Greek into modified Latin before settling into English almost unchanged.
clues: This condition of the mind takes its name from an ancient Greek verb meaning 'to remember,' with a tiny prefix attached that cancels that meaning out.
It is the loss of memory, often after injury or illness, far beyond everyday forgetfulness: a person may lose whole stretches of their past or even their identity.
A staple of soap operas and spy thrillers, it strikes Jason Bourne, who wakes with no idea who he is. Doctors speak of retrograde and anterograde types.
